title: Founders' Day

pages.text:
*From the Dropout Club Handbook, Rule 10: Sit at the back, near the exit, and close to the snacks.*

The morning air at Humbleton smelled of lavender and polished brass. Bunting hung so low it brushed the noses of the early arrivals. A brass band played on a platform. They were playing three different tunes at once. It made everyone around them look slightly dizzy.

The Dropout Club arrived together. They felt very small and very important. Toby wore his bow tie. He had polished it with a cloth until it shone like a wet river stone. Lulu had on her one matching pair of socks. It was a miracle she had been humming about since breakfast. Bunt had tied his giant red-spotted handkerchief over his nose. He looked less like a student and more like a very large, mossy outlaw.

Marnie walked with her head high. Her heart was doing somersaults. Perched on top of her copper-red buns was Gerald. He sat there with his orange beak tucked into his feathers. He looked every inch the hat Marnie had accidentally made him. He looked dignified. He looked ready for a ceremony. He did not look like a goose, unless you knew him well. Marnie did.
pages.image: Four students entering a wizard school courtyard: a girl with copper-red buns carrying Gerald on her head, a boy with glasses and a shiny bow tie, a girl in an orange hoodie, and a large troll with a handkerchief over his nose.

pages.text:
Principal Thistlewood stood on the stage, looking deeply uncomfortable. His tall purple hat was there, but it was far too small. It sat on his head like a lid on a saucepan, held in place by seven shiny silver pins that stuck out at odd angles.

"Precision above all!" he announced, his voice booming. "The art of magic is the art of never, ever being wrong!"

As he spoke, his moustache lifted off his lip. It hovered there for a second, twitching, before he quickly pressed it down with his finger. Marnie watched the movement and felt a strange prickling in her chest. It was not fear. It was the sharp, cold feeling of knowing you have broken a precious thing. She looked up at the hat. This was not the hat that had turned into a goose. This was the ordinary, stiff hat that had been there before.

A flicker of guilt crossed her face, quick and quiet, like a shadow passing over a sunbeam. She looked away, focusing instead on the cake table behind him, where pastries were arranged in perfect rows of size. She tried to remember why she felt so bad about a piece of purple wool.
pages.image: A tall, thin principal with a curled white moustache stands on a stage, wearing a comically small purple hat secured by multiple pins, while a girl in the crowd looks up at him with a thoughtful expression, with Gerald nearby.

pages.text:
The Great Hall was packed with students in gold-trimmed cloaks. They sat in rows that were so straight you could have drawn a line through them with a ruler. Cassius Pomeroy was at the front. His hair was slicked back, his blazer was crisp, and he held a golden notebook in his hands like a sacred text.

The Hall went silent. The silence was so heavy it felt like wool.

In the back, near the exit, Bunt shifted his weight. He was rubbing his nose with one massive finger. A tiny itch was starting to crawl up his nostrils. He looked at Toby, his eyes wide and worried.

Toby reached out and gently held Bunt’s arm. He did not say a word. He just squeezed, his grip firm and steady.

"Not yet," Toby whispered, his eyes fixed on the stage. He knew what was coming. He could feel the air in the room growing thick and perfect, a stillness that demanded attention. Bunt stopped rubbing his nose. He took a deep breath through his mouth, trying to keep the sneeze at bay.
pages.image: A crowded hall with students in gold cloaks sitting in straight rows; a boy with glasses gently holds the arm of a large troll who is rubbing his nose, while a boy in a blue blazer stands at the front.

pages.text:
Cassius stepped forward. He raised his silver wand, and for a moment, the only sound was the tick of the clock on the wall.

"Perfectus Universalis," he said.

A wave of gold glitter swept through the Hall. It moved like a slow, shimmering tide. Where it touched, things changed. The bunting straightened itself until it was taut and level. The brass band, which had been playing three different tunes, suddenly fell into perfect, synchronized harmony. Crumbs vanished from the floor. Every shoelace in the room tied itself into a neat, double bow.

The crowd gasped, then erupted in applause. It was the most beautiful thing they had ever seen. The Principal’s moustache rose again, this time staying up, curling into a perfect question mark of delight.

Marnie stood in the back, watching the glitter dance. She should have felt proud. She should have felt part of it. But as the gold light bathed her face, she felt a strange vibration in her bones, a hum that was not quite music and not quite sound.
pages.image: A wave of golden light sweeps through a hall, causing bunting to straighten and a band to play in sync; a girl with copper-red hair watches the shimmering light with a serious expression.

pages.text:
But the wave did not stop. It lingered in the air, a thick, golden mist that settled over the heads of the students. Then, with a soft *bong*, like a spoon striking a silver bell, something strange happened.

Little pointed red hats popped onto every head in the Hall.

Marnie blinked. She looked at where the Principal had been standing. There was no tall, thin man in a purple robe. Instead, there was a two-foot-tall figure with a long white beard, a bright blue jacket, and a fixed, cheerful smile painted on its face. It looked up at her with wide, surprised eyes.

He had become, quite perfectly, a garden gnome.

Marnie looked around. Every student, every teacher, every person who had been touched by that perfect gold light was now a small, smiling statue of clay. The only things that remained real were the four of them, standing in the back, looking very, very ordinary.
pages.image: A small, two-foot-tall garden gnome with a white beard and red hat stands on a stage, looking up at a girl with copper-red hair who is staring in shock; the background is filled with other small gnomes.
